messages:
maya: Heads up — seeing a bunch of requests that should match the header-override route but decision logs are empty for them. :eyes:
maya: Example trace: https://traces.internal/abc123 (span shows route match=true but no decision_log entry)
maya: Quick snippet from gateway logs:
```
INFO 2026-03-10T15:22:01Z route=match id=req-91 header:x-api-key=redacted
INFO 2026-03-10T15:22:01Z route=served id=req-91 model=redwood-llama-v1
// no decision_log emitted for req-91
```
raj: Are we sure sampling didn't drop those? last change to sampling config was last week right? :thinking_face:
sophia: I rolled the new sampling multipliers on Tue — global_decision_log_rate=0.02 but header_override_sample_boost should bump keys to 1.0. I verified the flag applied to the node pool.
oliver: Could be order-of-ops: we apply sampling check before header override rules are materialized in the eval context. If override isn't present yet, sampling thinks there's no match and drops logging.
maya: That matches the pattern — only requests with x-route-override show this gap. Non-override routes have expected logs. :bug:
raj: Can you paste the exact rule? might help repro.
maya: rule fragment:
```json
{"match": {"header": "x-route-override", "equals": "beta"}, "action": {"route": "beta-pool", "decision_log": "override"}}
```
sophia: I see — our evaluator adds `override` to request.meta in the post-match phase. sampling check runs at pre-match phase. Fix would be moving sampling evaluation to post-match (or making it accept future overrides).
oliver: Small patch idea: compute a "match preview" using header-only predicates and apply sampling after preview. Will open PR.
raj: Can we canary to a single node? prefer no global flip.
oliver: Yep, will target canary pool tag `canary-header-sampling` and set sampling to 100% there for a minute.
deploy-bot: deploy started: oliver/header-sampling-preview -> canary-header-sampling (build 8472) :rocket:
maya: I'll tail logs and watch decision_log metrics and trace coverage — will report after 5m.
(six minutes later)
maya: Canary looks clean — decision_log count for override routes jumped as expected. No regressions seen in latency. :thumbsup:
raj: Nice. oliver, want me to roll to rest of fleet?
oliver: Hold for one more hour while we run a quick hyposet of traffic with header permutations. Also adding a unit test for evaluator ordering.
sophia: Added metric alert for huge deltas in decision_log:route_coverage to catch regressions.
maya: Thanks all — filing follow-up to move sampling evaluation into post-match in the design doc: https://docs.internal/routing/ordering-proposal.
